answer: The thread detector writes to willow, and relic makes public every merge. A farm scripting its whole farm fires them together, thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 13 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 108 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 22 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
